newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt hopes for better ties with Khatami's Iran.
newsitem.headline: Egypt hopes for better ties with Khatami's Iran.

text.p: Egypt said on Wednesday it was looking forward to better ties with Tehran after positive remarks by Iran's newly elected President Mohammad Khatami.
"We're looking forward to good ties with Iran in light of the president-elect's remarks in which he lauded Egypt's role in the region," Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told reporters.
Khatami, a moderate Shi'ite cleric who was elected last week, said Iran disagreed with some of Egypt's policies but still respected "the great nation of Egypt".

Egypt has said Iran's alleged support of political violence stands in the way of a thaw in relations. It has accused Iran and Sudan of backing an attempt by Egyptian militants to kill President Hosni Mubarak in 1995. Both countries denied the charges.

Ties between Egypt and Iran began to deteriorate after Cairo signed a peace deal with Israel in 1979. Khatami also said it would be in the interest of both states to put their differences aside and work "hand in hand" against Israel, which he accused of sponsoring state terrorism.
Last month, Iran sent its foreign minister to invite Mubarak to an Islamic summit to be held in Tehran this year, a move described by analysts as an attempt to break the ice.
The visit by Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati was the first by a senior Iranian official since 1994.
